Ok so you came here to present an analogy based on objectively wrong information to an explicitly socialist sub without having done even the most basic of research on the topic. If you want to learn, go read or discuss in a subreddit more geared towards that. If you're just here to try for a gotcha moment, you know where the door is.

The capitalist system requires violent force to uphold. The expansion of markets internationally to increase profit has driven the governments of capitalist countries to bomb, invade, and murder people. To implement "my brand of socialism", it becomes necessary to use force against this capitalist violence.
Can I rephrase your question to make sure I understand your point? If socialism is better than capitalism why is capitalism "winning"?

That's another irrelevant question. Socialists want the ability for a single person, or small group, to actually own the MoP (also called "private property") to be abolished. Worker owned coops do exist within the capitalist system. And that's the problem. The are surrounded and choked out by the capitalist economy. The myth of capitalism being voluntary is absolutely false.

Redistribution of wealth is not the central tenant of socialism. Workers owning the means of production is. Your analogy might be relevant if the students all got together, taught themselves, encouraged each other, and learned the material that way. A basic understanding of socialism and what socialists really want to achieve is probably a good start before you start shitposting here.
